To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DNA mismatch repair (a process that corrects errors in DNA replication) activates a retrograde signaling pathway that leads to the activation of c-Abl, a protein kinase, which in turn phosphorylates and activates p73, a member of the tumor-suppressor p53 protein family, and GADD-45α, a proapoptotic protein, resulting in the activation of apoptosis (programmed cell death) in human cancer cells.
mismatch repair (MMH1) stimulates c-Abl/p53α/GADD45-mediated apoptosis, which is p53-independent.
MMR-dependent intrinsic apoptotic pathways are p53-independent, and are mediated by c-Abl/p53α/GADD45a retrograde signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the G2 checkpoint and apoptosis in response DNA damage.
the identification of the molecular pathways involved in DNA damage-induced cell death.
the identification of the retrograde (cytoplasm-to-nucleus) signal(s) that initiates MNR-dependent G2 arrest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MMR-dependent intrinsic apoptotic cell death is p53-independent and involves the retrograde (nuclear-to-cytoplamsic) c-Abl/p53/p73α/Gadd45α signaling pathway.
the hMLH1-c-Abl-p73α-GADD45α signaling pathway is a novel mechanism of intrinsic DNA damage-induced apoptosis.
MMR-dependent intrinsic (apoptotic) cell death is p53-independent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MMR-dependent cAbl/p73α/ GADD45α signaling induces apoptosis, but not cell cycle checkpoint arrest, in a p53-independent manner.
MMR-dependent G1/S checkpoint arrest and G2/M checkpoint arrest are p53-dependent, but MMR-dependent G _{2} /M checkpoint arrest is not.
hMLH1 is a key component of a novel DNA damage response pathway that involves the retrograde activation of c-Abl, which phosphorylates p73α, which in turn activates GADD45α to induce apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MMR-dependent intrinsic cell death is p53-independent but requires c-Abl-mediated retrograde signaling to p73α and subsequent GADD45α up-regulation.
MMR-deficient colon cancer cells are not resistant to cell death.
MMR-dependent G1 arrest is mediated by the p53 pathway and MMR-dependent G _{2} arrest is mediated by p73α.
